He was standing, listening to the trucks role passed his unfortunately placed motel room. The lights shimmer through the blinds as if the whole room was dirty, and being wiped by wiper blades. His room was dirty. He didn't dare think what it would be like under one of those black lights you see in the movies. Which walls would glow. Which fluids the splotches would represent. In fact he dared think and he found that regretful. He thought which would be better, to sleep in the bed or on the floor. Of course he knew that was reduculous and he would of course take the bed but he cringed for a second at the thought but reassured himself that the linens were likely the only thing cleaned in the room and are likely the best thing. He told himself this just because he knew he would not be able to sleep unless he put the thought out of his head.

Meanwhile truck after truck passed. He could tell if it would be a car long before he could hear it, as rare as that was, from the color of the light that shimmered in, which would appear and stay in one spot for a while before it shifted across the room at seemingly two distinct speeds. He could tell before it started moving. Each of the trucks had the exact same color and he knew that if there was any variation there would be a car next in the queue as they passed in almost rhythmic and even spaces. It was not as stochostic as he would expect for their distance. He would take that chance when identified to close his eyes knowing he would not flinch when it came by and imagined using the soft noise to help him sleep. He also reasured himself as they went by with a thought that continued quite passed the car's departure and went further down the line of reasoning each car that passed that maybe this place isn't so different. After all where are these cars coming from and going to. There must be houses near by. Maybe this town isn't so different from my own. Perhaps my own town when viewed with fresh eyes would have a sketchy ambiance that I would have never before noticed. An old torn down man at a gas station. That's something I could see in my own town and think nothing of it.

He thought about the people in those homes. If they were different from the people he grew up around his own town, if they were communting to typical office jobs in some unknown nearby town, or if they were radically different. Dark thoughts crepped into his head for a second. What if I went into one and just killed the family and took over the household? Sarcastically he though how long would it be before people asked questions? Surely just days. The prospect seemed hardly a solution. And truely it wasn't besides the fact he would never do that. He just wanted to think of any solution to his predicament and no brainstorm was out of question. It could at least be thought about just as an exercise. Getting familiar with thinking about his problem and the intricisies. After all maybe a bad idea can be molded into a good one with time. Who knows but the solution that really get's me out of this could be birthed from an originally bad idea evolved as a product of necessity. No idea was bad to think about because he only needed one, the right one. Hundreds of ideas would pass before he found it. Perhaps it wouldn't require him to sacrifice any of his morals. He knew that failing to think about it would not take him any further along his journey and only make it more enevitable that such a mystic solution would not be found.

He also knew he needed to sleep and that stress would not help him get his head together any better than it had been the last few days, which to be fair was a complete mess and only seemed to be getting worse.
